# October

## Debiased Machine Learning (BIP Project)

Debiased / Double Machine Learning (DML) is a semiparametric estimation method that came out of the economics literature that allows us to obtain an unbiased and efficient estimate for a low-dimensional target parameter $\psi$ (perhaps to do statistical inference) while accounting for high-dimensional nuisance parameters $\eta$. However, they have become useful in biostatistics. Example: Jinbo paper.

\textbf{Q1}. What is the simplest framework that we are familiar with: Partial Linear Regression (generalized additive model type thing?) and a connection to the Frisch-Waugh-Lovell theorem we know from linear models.

$$
Y \sim X + \boldsymbol{f}(\boldsymbol{V})
$$

This function is infinite-dimensional (a thought exercise and an informal proof in linear algebra).

\textbf{Q2}. How do we estimate this infinite-dimensional nuisance with the data? Machine Learning!

The double part of this method is that we use two separate machine learning models for the partial Y and partial X (notated as D in these papers)

\textbf{Thought: What might go wrong with just fitting a machine learning model on this equation?}

\textbf{Q3}. Machine learning methods are a black box... how do we confirm we obtain an unbiased estimate of our target parameter(s)?: Neyman Orthogonality. There is some detail that I don't know if I can go into in time...
